name: org.machanism.machai:bindex-core
description: Bindex Core is a Java 17 library for creating, validating, registering, retrieving, and semantically recommending Bindex metadata. A Bindex descriptor describes a reusable software artifact with Maven coordinates, licensing, authorship, classification, API features, configuration, and practical usage guidance. Bindex Core provides an AI-facing FunctionTools implementation that MCP-compatible hosts can publish to retrieve a descriptor by coordinates, URL, or local file; select libraries from a natural-language requirement using embedding and MongoDB vector search; and register descriptors from a file, URL, or JSON object. Its core services persist Bindex documents and classification embeddings in MongoDB, resolve dependencies, and support AI-assisted project assembly and library discovery.

constructors.description: Creates the AI tool provider that exposes Bindex retrieval, recommendation, registration, schema, and generation-prompt capabilities. Repository access is initialized lazily from the host configurator when a repository-backed tool is called.

examples.description: Create the tool provider when embedding Bindex capabilities in a Java AI-tool host. The host discovers its annotated tool methods.

constructors.description: Creates the core registration and semantic-selection service with a repository and application configuration.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexRepository repository = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.MongoBindexRepository(configurator);
org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker picker = new org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.Picker(repository, configurator);
examples.description: Create a MongoDB-backed picker in an application that owns the configurator and repository lifecycle.

features.name: get-bindex
features.signature: public org.machanism.machai.schema.Bindex org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools.getBindex(java.lang.String id, java.lang.String query, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: AI functional tool that loads a Bindex descriptor by registered identifier, HTTP(S) URL, or file URI. A GraphQL-style selection query can reduce the returned top-level fields.

examples.description: Read and validate a project-local descriptor while requesting only identity and classification fields.

features.name: pick-libraries
features.signature: public java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> org.machanism.machai.bindex.ai.tools.BindexFunctionTools.getRecommendedLibraries(java.lang.String prompt, double score, int vectorSearchLimits, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: AI functional tool that classifies a natural-language requirement, creates an embedding, and returns semantically relevant registered libraries. Tool defaults are a 0.85 minimum score and 25 results.

examples.snippet: java.util.Collection<org.machanism.machai.bindex.core.BindexInfo> matches = tools.getRecommendedLibraries("Java library metadata search for an MCP agent", 0.85d, 25, configurator);
examples.description: Ask the catalog for libraries relevant to an MCP-enabled Java metadata-search solution.

examples.name: Publish Bindex tools through an MCP server
examples.description: 1. Install Java 17 or newer and download machai-mcp-server.jar and bindex-core.jar. 2. Configure GENAI_USERNAME, GENAI_PASSWORD, gw.model, embedding.model, and MongoDB settings as required by the environment. 3. Start the MCP server with bindex-core on its classpath. 4. Connect an MCP client and invoke get-bindex, pick-libraries, or a registration tool.
examples.notes: Use a semicolon instead of a colon between JAR files on Windows. See https://machai.machanism.org/bindex-core/functional-tools.html for tool details.

examples.name: Use as a Maven dependency
examples.description: 1. Add the dependency to a Maven project. 2. Supply the required GenAI and MongoDB configuration through the application or MCP host. 3. Create BindexFunctionTools or publish the JAR through the Machai MCP Server. 4. Use the discovery and registration functions in a real catalog workflow.
examples.notes: Snapshot availability depends on the configured Maven repository.
